best_for: Windows and Mac users with a Microsoft account who want Desktop, Documents and photos backed up and reachable on every device, and who will pay for more space once 5 GB runs out.

points.title: 5 GB free, shared with your mail
points.text: A free Microsoft account comes with 5 GB of cloud storage. That space also holds Outlook.com attachments, so a busy inbox eats into what is left for files.

points.title: Going over the limit is serious
points.text: Over quota, OneDrive turns read-only and stops syncing new files, and Outlook.com stops sending and receiving mail. After three months the account is frozen, and after six months Microsoft may delete the files for good.

points.title: Paying for room
points.text: Microsoft 365 Basic gives 100 GB for one person, plus ad-free Outlook, ransomware detection and recovery, and no file cap in Personal Vault. Larger Microsoft 365 plans add more storage and the Office apps.

points.title: Files on demand save disk space
points.text: Files can stay online-only and take no local space, download when opened, or be kept on the device for offline use. On Windows this needs Windows 10 version 1709 or later, and some third-party antivirus tools can get in the way.

points.title: Current systems only
points.text: Microsoft lists Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 for the sync app; support for Windows 10 21H2 and older ended on August 15, 2026. On a Mac it asks for macOS 15.8 or newer and a case-insensitive APFS drive.

points.title: No Linux client
points.text: OneDrive is listed here for Windows and macOS only, and Microsoft's requirements page covers no Linux desktop app.

points.title: Per-user or per-machine on Windows
points.text: Windows installers come in per-user and machine-wide forms for x86, x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 110 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so a Mac downgrade needs another source.
